dates.display: c.1621×1623–1641 (West Barsham wardship of Edward Gournay)

incoming.explanation: Kin-sourced through Anne (Lewkenor) L'Estrange, the jest-book adds family-tradition context to the West Barsham terminal pedigree the wardship records set out - corroborating Edward Gournay's marriage to Frances Hovell while confirming that the erroneous '1614' death for Thomas III circulated as family tradition.

outgoing.explanation: The WARD 7 / C 142 inquisitions establish the wardship that put the minor heir's household under Court of Wards administration in the emigration decade.

shortLabel: West Barsham wardship: Edward Gournay a minor ward to c.1628 (WARD 7 / C 142)

sources.alignmentNote: Brass names Edward son and heir of Thomas Gournay Esq. and Martha daughter of Sir Edward Lewkenor of Denham, d. Aug 1641.
sources.locator: vol. 5, Gallow Hundred, West Barsham parish (Edward Gournay chancel brass)

sources.alignmentNote: Variant 'Edmund / Frances Hovell / heir aged nine' reading of the terminal generation, unreconciled with the brass; recorded, not resolved.
Establishes Thomas Gurney III alive in 1621, dying vita patris 1621×1623; Edward therefore a minor at his 1623 succession. Fuller treatment on the G15 companion (lead L-113).

sources.alignmentNote: Catalogue descriptions read at TNA Discovery; WARD 7 is a Court of Wards series, implying a wardship of the minor heir. Documents not yet pulled.

statement: The West Barsham heir was a royal ward through the later 1620s. Thomas Gurney III (Henry G15's eldest son, m. Martha Lewkenor of Denham) died in his father's lifetime, c.1621×1623 — Henry G15's will of 1 May 1621 still names 'my eldest sonne Thomas' among the living — and Henry himself died in 1623, so his grandson and heir Edward Gournay (b. 1608) succeeded as a minor: a ward of the Crown under his widowed mother Martha, coming of age about 1628. Edward held West Barsham to his death on 6 August 1641 (inquisition C 142/613/60). Earlier 'Gurney, Thomas: Norfolk' entries in the Court of Wards series (WARD 7/57/157, /80, 1616/17–1617/18) cannot be Thomas III's death inquisitions — he was living in 1621 — and are carried only as unresolved catalogue leads.
